# Your reading account

Every page here has a price of a few pence, and you pay for the share of it you read: scroll a tenth of the way down and you pay a tenth. You started with £5.00 of credit. If a page was not worth it, say so at its foot and it is not charged. What you read is also what builds your graph below, and your [newsroom](newsroom.md): a front page for each of your [personas](personas.md).

**Where your data is kept.** Your balance, history and receipts are kept in this browser’s storage, and your reading is not sent anywhere unless you choose to send it. There is no account. This is a client-side application: the pages are static files, with no server of ours behind them for now, and if encrypted vaults are added this page will say so. [Why it is built this way](../articles/no-server-by-design.md).

A new browser, a private window or clearing site data starts again with £5.00 and no history. Credit can go below zero, and no page is blocked.

What can leave your browser, when you choose to, is a payment (made on Stripe’s own page), a subscription or a reading share: [what leaves your browser, and when](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/shipped/index.html#data). [How the meter works](../meter/index.md), and [why it works this way](../articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.md).

The reading account needs JavaScript: it lives in your browser and nowhere else.

## What things cost, read to the end

| Page | Price |
|---|---|
| An article published in the last seven days | 10p |
| An older article | 5p |
| A newsletter issue | 3p |
| A desk note | 2p |
| A collection | 2p |
| Any other page that charges: an article's version history, the newsroom's roles and policies | 1p |
| The front page, the subscribe page, your account, the design, replicate and persona pages | free |

The price of a page read to the end; you pay that times the share you scrolled through, never less than a tenth. One charge per page per browser session: reading further later tops the same charge up, and going back costs nothing more. Reading the markdown twin of a page, or the newsroom wire, is not metered.

## Why it works like this

To find out whether people pay for reading, a few pence at a time, when nothing forces them to and what they get back is a site that knows what they read and picks for them, with no account and nobody else holding the history. The plan, the numbers we expect and the date we check them are in [going live with the reading meter](../articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.md); who could cheat it, and why that is allowed, is in [who will game the reading meter](../articles/who-will-game-the-reading-meter.md).
